newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin stable in hospital, working on papers.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin stable in hospital, working on papers.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin's health "stabilised significantly" on Thursday, a Kremlin spokesman said, adding that the president, who is in hospital with pneumonia, had spent two hours working on papers during the day.

"The patient's condition has stabilised significantly. His temperature and blood pressure are normal. An X-ray has shown progress in curing the pneumonia," the spokesman told Reuters, reading from a prepared statement.
"Today the president worked on documents for two hours, paying special attention to preparing a state of the nation address to parliament."
The Kremlin statement added that Yeltsin's wife, Naina, who has also been ill, had been discharged from the Central Clinical Hospital.

The 65-year-old president is expected to remain there for the rest of the week. Yeltsin was taken into the elite clinic on January 8, just two weeks after returning to the Kremlin following a heart bypass operation in November.

Doctors say the pneumonia in both lungs has no direct link to the heart surgery, but the cardiologist who conducted the bypass operation is a permanent member of the medical team treating Yeltsin at present.
Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov warned on Wednesday that pneumonia was a serious condition which could lead to complications and needed careful treatment.
